title: I Worked for a Whole Day Using Only the iPhone Duo. Here’s How It Went
gist: Wired's Julian Chokkattu wrote his iPhone Duo review entirely on Apple's $1,999 first foldable, finding light work doable with a kickstand and keyboard despite iOS multitasking limits and unoptimized third-party apps. Battery hit about 45 percent at 6 pm after roughly six hours of screen-on time.

insights.claim: The iPhone Duo costs $1,999, close to the combined price of an iPhone 18 Pro ($1,199) and an iPad ($449), framing it as a two-in-one device.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Apple's first foldable is priced at a premium that must be justified by replacing two devices.

insights.claim: The author concludes the Duo will not replace a laptop and may feel cramped to iPad users, but focused light work is entirely doable with a kickstand and portable keyboard.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Positions the Duo as a productivity supplement rather than a PC replacement.
insights.locator: You probably won’t want to replace your laptop

insights.claim: The author wonders whether a single do-it-all device is as great as it is chalked up to be compared with dedicated devices.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: A skeptical note on device convergence that could temper foldable demand.
insights.locator: Maybe we’ll realize a single do-it-all device

insights.claim: iOS does not recognize a Bluetooth mouse or trackpad by default; users must enable AssistiveTouch in accessibility settings to get an iPad-like cursor.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Input friction hampers the Duo's workstation use case relative to iPad.
insights.locator: Notably, iOS doesn’t recognize a Bluetooth mouse

insights.claim: Apple imposes multitasking restrictions on the Duo: split screen is only an equal 50-50 split, and in portrait only video apps can pin to the top with another app below.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Software limits, not hardware, constrain Apple's foldable productivity pitch.
insights.locator: Apple also imposes arbitrary multitasking restrictions

insights.claim: The author wants a Slide Over-style feature on the Duo to hide floating messaging apps like Slack, WhatsApp or Messages without disturbing split screen.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Feature request that could shape iOS updates for the Duo.
insights.locator: I still think Apple should add a feature like

insights.claim: Apple's app pairs let users pin two apps together in Recents, which the author says Apple got right.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: A bright spot in the Duo's multitasking software.
insights.locator: One thing Apple did get right is app pairs.

insights.claim: Most apps are not optimized for the Duo and could take weeks or months to look right; Slack updated the day before testing for the larger screen, while Zoom and most Google Workspace apps looked poor.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: App ecosystem optimization lag is a launch-window friction for the Duo.
insights.locator: The app that annoyed me the most was Gmail.

insights.claim: Google updated the Google Search app for the Duo early in launch week and the author expects fuller support soon, possibly by the Friday launch.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Developer support should improve quickly after launch.
insights.locator: I imagine full support will come very soon

insights.claim: By 6 pm the Duo's battery was around 45 percent after about six hours of screen-on time, which the author calls very impressive.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Strong battery life removes a common foldable weakness.
insights.locator: By 6 pm, battery life was sitting around 45 percent

insights.claim: The author expects compact keyboards from makers like Nillkin and ProtoArc, plus MagSafe kickstands and cases, to serve workers using the Duo everywhere, and notes Apple Pencil support arrives later this year.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Accessory demand could be a second-order beneficiary of the Duo.
insights.locator: I imagine we'll see an array of compact keyboards
